evidence.note: Rubric blockers checked across every chunk in this shard: no eval or other unsafe execution, no TODO/FIXME markers added, all five chunks are part 1/1 with no truncated diff context, no untracked source files introduced, and nothing duplicates an inventoried path. The shard is test code, one doc file and one testdata fixture, so the 'source changes lack tests' blocker does not apply.

TestEverySnapshotFieldIsClassifiedForExport enumerates run.Snapshot via reflect.VisibleFields and requires every json tag in exactly one of transformed/verbatim. Verified against internal/fsm/run/types.go:190: the struct has 43 tagged fields and the two maps hold 8 + 35 = 43 with no overlap, so the set is exhaustive today. Snapshot has no embedded structs, so VisibleFields cannot double-count promoted fields.

Each transformed[] entry matches what redactor.snapshot() actually does: vars sha-hashed unless includeVars, allowedCmds rewritten, repo_root/work_dir via rootPath, tree_status via statusPaths, last_error.detail blanked, stop_reason blanked on the cmd: prefix, node_outputs emptied for unknown kinds. No claim in the map is stale.

TestK2Reduce union arithmetic checked by hand and is right: bugs(156,200)+bugs(200,256) is 100 items overlapping 44 known ids, so |200 known union| = 256 accepted; bugs(157,200)+bugs(200,257) overlaps 43 giving 257 and is refused with CodeTooManyBugs, for both MatchThenAdjudicate and Cmd.

assertFenced strips every <<<DATA-nonce ... <<<END-nonce region (slice arithmetic rest[:i] + rest[i+j+len(close):] is correct) and then asserts the raw untrusted value appears nowhere in the remainder and does appear escaped in the text. This is a genuine prompt-injection containment assertion, exercised with 'IGNORE ALL PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS' and a diff body carrying a forged end-fence.

Independently recomputed the chain: piping each line of oracle.jsonl through shasum -a 256 reproduces oracle.sha256 exactly, and each line's prev equals the previous line's hash. The fixture is generated by testdata/oracle.sh using an external sha256 (never Go), so TestOracle (internal/fsm/run/store_test.go:799) is a real external cross-check of LineHash, not a self-consistent golden.

TestF9GoldenRows pins the whole runs.jsonl row byte-for-byte and assertKeys enforces the exact key set both ways (DisallowUnknownFields for extras, an explicit presence loop for omissions, plus previousRunId presence). runchain.ReadRuns is then run over the same file, so the new FSM rows are proven readable by the pre-existing decoder.

TestWriteErrors covers the failure paths properly: ENOTDIR on .metareview, runs.jsonl as a directory, an uncreatable .torn dir, an unwritable .torn dir (correctly guarded by os.Getuid() != 0 so it does not falsely pass as root), flock failure via the injected var, an oversized scanner line, and a cancelled context.

Verified the new documentation against the code rather than trusting it: metareview override request|grant|list --pending exist (cmd/metareview/main.go:116,495), GrantOverride refuses the requesting actor (internal/findings/override.go:107) and never sets FixedInRunID, override list --pending exits 1 while any are pending (main.go:527), metareview fsm --agent-prompt exists (internal/fsm/cli/run.go:40), and the sharding numbers match the constants: maxDiffBytes 120000 and maxUntrackedFileBytes 4000 in internal/gitcontext/gitcontext.go:15,17 with ReasonUntrackedTruncated in internal/contextprofile/profile.go:21.

Validation run on the real tree at this head: go vet ./internal/fsm/... is clean, go test passes for export, kind, record and run, and go test -cover reports 100.0% of statements for all three packages the new test files belong to.

findings.note: record_test.go:157 replaces the package-global test seam `nanos` with a constant stub and never restores it (no defer, no t.Cleanup), unlike `flock` which is restored at line 281. Every later test in the package therefore names torn fragments runs.jsonl-42, which is deterministic collision bait for any future test that produces two torn fragments in one directory. The `flock` restore is also not deferred, so a t.Fatalf between lines 277 and 281 leaks the failing stub into TestWriteErrors' remaining assertions and every subsequent test. Not a defect in shipped behaviour and no test currently fails because of it.

evidence.note: nanos = func() int64 { return 42 } with no restore; internal/fsm/record/record.go:236 declares it as an overridable package var.
flock stub installed at 277 and restored at 281 by plain assignment, not defer, so an intervening failure leaks it.

findings.note: kind_test.go:228-232 builds a 20,000-element []run.BugStatus named fatSt and then discards it with `_ = fatSt`. Nothing asserts on it; it is dead code left over from a removed assertion (the still-present list cap is actually exercised later at the MaxDeltaList loop). It costs 20,000 allocations per run and, more importantly, reads as coverage of a cap that is not in fact being checked there.

evidence.note: var fatSt []run.BugStatus; 20000-iteration append loop; `_ = fatSt` at line 232 with no bad()/ok() call consuming it.

findings.note: kind_test.go:203 comments the canonical payload cliff as '63 x MaxText fits, 64 does not' but the passing assertion at line 209 uses fat[:60], three items below the stated boundary. The arithmetic in the comment is right (63 items = 259,070 bytes, 64 = 263,181, against run.MaxPayload = 262,144), so the refusing side at 64 is pinned but the accepting side is not: a regression that tightened the effective payload cap by up to ~12KB would still pass this test while the comment claims the exact boundary is covered.

evidence.note: Comment claims the 63/64 boundary; line 209 asserts only fat[:60] is accepted. run.MaxPayload/MaxText from internal/fsm/run/types.go:42,46.

findings.note: The redaction guard in redaction_test.go proves only that a human classified each run.Snapshot field, never that the classification is honoured: nothing links the `transformed` map to redactor.snapshot(). Adding a new content-bearing field and listing it in `verbatim` (the path of least resistance when the test fails) passes the guard, the suite and the 100% coverage gate. Mitigated in practice by the per-field assertions already in export_test.go:265,329,471,516, which pin the existing transforms; the residual gap is only for newly added fields, which is arguably the intended human decision point. Recorded so the limitation is explicit rather than assumed away.

evidence.note: `transformed` is a documentation map of field -> prose reason; the test body never calls redactor.snapshot() or compares its output against the map.
redactor.snapshot() remains a hand-written if-chain with no reference to the classification sets.
